title: U.S. House · Oklahoma's 2nd District
area: Eastern Oklahoma, including Muskogee, McAlester and the Cherokee, Choctaw and Muscogee reservation areas

candidates.name: Josh Brecheen

summary.text: Josh Brecheen is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Oklahoma's 2nd District, a former Oklahoma state senator, seeking re-election.

background.text: Born in Pontotoc County, Oklahoma; graduated from Coalgate High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Oklahoma State University.
Career experience includes operating a heavy equipment and trucking business, working as a field representative for former U.S. Senator Tom Coburn, and ranching.
Served as state president of the Oklahoma FFA Association.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Budget Committee and the House Homeland Security Committee, where he is a member of the Emergency Management and Technology Subcommittee and chairman of the Oversight, Investigations, and Accountability Subcommittee.

priorities.text: Lists deficit spending, border security, traditional values, constitutional adherence and energy dominance as his legislative priorities.

positions.summary: His official site says he supports stopping government subsidies for green energy and cutting regulations on oil and natural gas producers.
positions.quote: we need to stop government subsidies for green energy and cut the burdensome regulations placed on oil and natural gas producers.

positions.summary: In a November 2025 statement he welcomed Border Patrol agents releasing no illegal immigrants back into the country.
positions.quote: US Border Patrol agents releasing ZERO illegal aliens back into America. This is great news!!!

candidates.researchNotes: Key floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately. His official site lists legislative priority categories (deficit spending, border security, traditional values, constitutional adherence, energy dominance) without accompanying position statements or press releases explaining each in detail; only border security could be tied to a specific documented action (current committee assignment).

candidates.name: Brandon Wade

summary.text: Brandon Wade is a union committee chairman in the oil industry from Washington County, running as the Democratic candidate on a message of bipartisan representation and protecting reproductive rights.

background.text: Born in Bartlesville, Oklahoma; earned a high school diploma from Copan High School.
Career experience as a laborer in the oil industry; has served as union committee chairman and executive board member (Vice President) for IUOE Local 351.

priorities.text: "Returning Real Representation to our Congress" by listening to voters of all parties rather than following party lines.
priorities.quote: Returning Real Representation to our Congress. To do this we must listen to all voters, from all parties.

positions.summary: His campaign site says Roe v. Wade should be codified into federal law and that no one should face prosecution for seeking or receiving health care.
positions.quote: I believe Roe v. Wade should be codified into federal law to guarantee the right to privacy in healthcare decisions.

positions.summary: His campaign site calls for a nationwide system providing affordable healthcare to every U.S. citizen, naming a Medicare for All approach among models to explore.
positions.quote: Develop a nationwide system that provides affordable healthcare to every U.S. citizen.

positions.summary: His campaign site calls for reforming the tax system so the wealthy and large corporations pay more, with a corporate rate between 21% and 28%.
positions.quote: Reform the tax system so the wealthy and large corporations pay their fair share.

positions.summary: His campaign site says current tariff policies raise costs for everyday Americans and calls for replacing them with other policy.
positions.quote: Current tariff policies are increasing costs for everyday Americans.

positions.summary: His campaign site calls for federal and state education funds to go to public schools rather than private institutions.
positions.quote: Ensure federal and state funds are directed to public schools, not diverted to private institutions.

positions.summary: A 2023-era issues page (it cites fourteen years without an increase since 2009) says the minimum wage must be raised and calls for moving it to $16.00 immediately.
positions.quote: We must continue to demand the minimum wage be raised.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website located; positions drawn from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.
